title: JANUS Engine R0 — Rotating Gill Ring oxygen-extraction gate
goal: Determine the real oxygen extraction rate of a rotating annular biomimetic gill before making any engine power or self-support claims.
core_question: How many milligrams of O2 per second can a rotating gill ring extract from water as a function of ring diameter, active membrane area, RPM, water speed, dissolved oxygen concentration, temperature, pressure and collector-side oxygen activity?

physics_model.combined_relative_speed_candidate: v_rel ~= sqrt(v_water^2 + v_tip^2) as a first geometric bound only; actual local flow field must be measured or CFD-resolved
physics_model.engine_ceiling_rule: Any engine-power estimate must be downstream of measured m_dot_O2 and oxygen stoichiometry; no power claim may be inferred from membrane area or RPM alone.

minimum_mass_balance.collector_side: m_dot_O2_collected must independently agree with water-side oxygen loss within declared uncertainty

baseline_test_matrix.note: These are candidate characterization points, not prescribed safe operating limits. Structural RPM limits must be established separately for the real prototype material and geometry.
controls: same ring with collector gradient disabled or equilibrated
blank water-loop oxygen loss test without gill membrane

success_metrics.primary: reproducible positive O2 mass flow with independent mass-balance closure
secondary: oxygen flux versus dissolved oxygen concentration
watts consumed per mg/s O2 captured
evidence for or against boundary-layer thinning from rotation

failure_modes_to_watch: rotation improves mixing but drive power costs more energy than useful oxygen capture justifies
membrane-side depletion remains dominant despite RPM increase
collector-side pO2 rises and collapses the diffusion gradient
gas bubble nucleation creates false oxygen collection readings
biofouling or particulate fouling reduces flux
centrifugal stress damages membrane or seals
apparent oxygen loss is caused by degassing rather than membrane transfer
next_gate: R0A_GEOMETRY_FREEZE: choose one ring diameter and active membrane geometry from the JANUS Axle-derived form; then build a non-combustion water-loop test article and measure O2 flux versus RPM and water speed before integrating condenser or engine functions.
